title: strictgen config
description: The strictgen.json file that drives strictgen. Paths are relative to the folder that holds the config file. Only the targets listed under targets are generated.

$schema.description: The JSON Schema of this file, for editors. Ignored by strictgen.

schemas.description: The folder the JSON Schemas are read from. Every *.json file directly in it is one schema.

idBase.description: The base every schema $id starts with: a schema in <file>.json must have the $id <idBase><file>.json. When left out, it is taken from the first schema by file name.

ids.description: Selects the defs that become ID types: every def of the schema file `file` whose name ends in `suffix`. Left out, no def becomes an ID type.

file.description: The schema file name, without .json, like common.

suffix.description: The def name suffix, like Id, so orderId is an ID.

header.description: The first line of every generated file, written as a comment. Files that start with it are the ones removed from a shared folder before writing. One line, no control characters.
header.default: Code generated by strictgen. DO NOT EDIT.

validation.description: Not yet active. Turns constraint checks on in every decoder.

targets.description: The languages to generate. Only the targets listed here are written, and at least one is needed.

llm.description: Not yet active. LLM structured output profiles.

profiles.description: The provider profiles to generate, like openai.

out.description: The folder the provider-ready schemas are written to.

cleanup.description: Fixes common syntax mistakes, like a surrounding code fence, before LLM decoding.

docs.description: Not yet active. A documentation page per type.

out.description: The folder the pages are written to.

format.description: Not yet active. The formatter run on each language's output when it is installed.

out.description: A folder the target writes to, relative to the config file.

read.description: Not yet active. strict rejects unknown keys, report accepts them and reports their paths.

rust.description: The Rust target: a module per schema, a helpers module and mod.rs, which re-exports every type.

out.description: The folder the Rust modules are written to, like src/generated. strictgen owns it: it is cleared before writing.

fixtures.description: The fixture registry, a Rust test file that decodes each fixture folder with the type generated for it. false or left out writes none.

out.description: The folder registry.rs is written to, like tests/generated. strictgen owns it.

crate.description: The Rust path the registry reaches the generated types by, like my_types or my_types::generated.

allow.description: The lints mod.rs allows for every generated module, each with its reason. Replaces the default list.

reason.description: Why generated code can't avoid the lint.

default.reason: descriptions come from the schemas, which name keys without backticks
variant names come from schema values, which often share a prefix
variants follow the schemas, only recursive ones are boxed

embedSchemas.description: Also writes schemas.rs, declared as pub mod schemas: every schema as minified ASCII JSON, so a Rust validator can load them without file access.

go.description: The Go target: a file per schema and helpers.go, all in one package, plus registry_test.go for fixture tests and a .gitattributes that marks the generated files.

out.description: The folder of the Go package.

package.description: The Go package name, a Go identifier that isn't a keyword.

shared.description: true when the folder also holds hand written files, like go.mod and tests: only the files that start with the header are removed before writing. false clears the whole folder.

typescript.description: The TypeScript target: a file per schema and index.ts, which re-exports every type.

out.description: The folder the TypeScript files are written to. strictgen owns it: it is cleared before writing.

decoders.description: Not yet active. Generates a strict decoder per type.
